mece.finding: MECE over the declared domain, by subtraction from a printed denominator of SIX values (the five guard thresholds DB-b-118 placed, plus tieout_tolerance_proposed). The five are placed by DB-b-118 and are not re-opened. The sixth, tieout_tolerance_proposed, has exactly the routes the four members name: a number given to the writer by the tie-out cell (--tieout) that the writer neither measured nor derived is `held` (the contract already says DB-b-3 PROPOSES it and the writer only carries it); a number the writer computes from its own data would be `measured` and none does; a number derived from other values by a stated rule would be `inferred` and none is; no number is `absent` (Cottonwood, where no tie-out has been run). Six values minus those routes leaves ZERO unplaced, and the member `absent` is exercised by the null the column already can hold. The claim set is NOT widened: THRESHOLD_CLAIMS stays the same four members, so the sixth value takes the same claim, not a fifth way of knowing. Listing row 3 adds a ROW to method_versions (a second positive: method_version 3 beside 1 and 2) and adds no member to any enum: the contract's enums block, which holds method, flow_convention, income_basis, fee_basis, day_count, threshold_claims and threshold_claims_source, is unchanged by it. Stated limit: this subtraction is over the values the method row WRITES today (denominator 6), not over every field a future method row could carry.

intent_coherence.finding: INTENT COHERENCE. The claim column answers one question, 'how does the writer know this value', which is the question the five claim columns answer; it is not a quality count or a per-account fact, so it stays inside the table's one question (what arithmetic produced the numbers that point at it). The tie-out value is a statement ABOUT the method (a tolerance proposed for graded tie-outs), not a return, so it already belongs on this row; the claim does not add a second intent. Row 3 serves the same intent as rows 1 and 2: it states the arithmetic that produced the returns pointing at method_version 3, with the fields the row leaves to the source entry named as such rather than invented.

state_coherence.finding: STATE COHERENCE (which values one remedy does NOT move). Filling the tie-out (a run of the tie-out cell, passing --tieout) moves tieout_tolerance_proposed and its claim together and moves none of the five thresholds, their claims or threshold_claims_source; re-measuring the thresholds moves none of the tie-out pair. The ratified tieout_tolerance and its ruling are untouched by either. A claim the input does not state is defaulted by the DB-b-118 rule (null reads absent, a value reads held), and a caller that passes five stated threshold claims and no tie-out claim keeps working unchanged: its tie-out claim is defaulted, and threshold_claims_source still describes only the five. Adding row 3 to method_versions moves no row-1 or row-2 field, and the thresholds, which the entry and the thresholds file own, are not asserted for row 3. landed_row (the version-1 partition as read) is not touched.

No enum member is added: the claim values are the four of enums.threshold_claims. Stated with its limit: this is a name census of what this cell introduces, not a census of the estate.

decision: (1) The claim is one flat string column tieout_tolerance_proposed_claim, in THRESHOLD_CLAIMS, non-nullable. (2) A stated threshold_claims object MAY carry the key tieout_tolerance_proposed and then the same rules bind: a claim outside the set refuses, a null only under absent, a value never under absent. (3) When it does not carry the key, the DB-b-118 no-claims rule is applied to this one value: null reads absent, a value reads held, so five stated claims with no tie-out keeps working. (4) tieout_tolerance_proposed is written as an arrow double so a null lands typed. (5) comparability() and the grading paths are untouched. (6) The contract goes to 0.5.0 with the new column, the nullable tie-out, method row 3, a recomputed schema_hash and a supersedes naming 0.4.0 and its hash.
